clue.text: Using the feet helps William bicycle

indicators.note: the two words help to make up the answer, each lending some of its letters to a run that hides inside them

explanation.surface: Pedalling a bike is something William does with his feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of 'William' and the start of 'bicycle'; 'helps' says those two words contribute it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse built from metrical feet of a short then long syllable is iambic, so it uses poetic feet.

clue.text: Provide help for Virginia in trouble

indicators.note: the state's abbreviation sits in the middle of the word meaning trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to aid Virginia in a time of difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail someone is to be of use or benefit to them, an old verb for giving assistance.

clue.text: Pack with joker available for the use of players

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing the noun: a vehicle meant for musicians

parts.note: a band is a group or gang, like a pack
a wag is a joker or wit
on means available, as a dish that is on the menu

explanation.surface: A deck of cards with a joker, ready for the card players to use.
explanation.walkthrough: Players are musicians here, not card players: the wagon carried the band in a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandwagon is a cart carrying a band of musicians in a procession.

clue.text: Boy, no Christian, rose to rule the world

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the god who rose up to take power over the universe

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters rise, so the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a boy is a son
O is zero, nothing, no amount
RC, Roman Catholic, is a kind of Christian

explanation.surface: A lad without a Christian faith climbs to world domination.
explanation.walkthrough: SON, O and RC give SONORC, which 'rose' turns upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan overthrew his father Uranus and was supreme ruler of the universe until Zeus deposed him.

clue.text: Pirate captain in an awkward spot — they are for hanging

indicators.note: the captain is placed inside the rearranged spot
awkward suggests the letters of spot are set out clumsily in a new order

parts.note: Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: A pirate chief finds himself in a tight corner, facing the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' gives POTS; 'in' signals the container. Captain Hook is the pirate of Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Pothooks are S-shaped hooks for hanging cooking pots over a fire.

clue.text: Vulgar fractions presumably out, of place in this abstract science

definitions.text: Vulgar fractions presumably out, of place in this abstract science

parts.words: Vulgar fractions presumably out, of place in this abstract science
parts.note: vulgar, meaning coarse, would be out of place in a branch of mathematics described by the opposite of coarse, so the joke plays on vulgar fractions

explanation.surface: Simple fractions seem not to belong in a theoretical branch of mathematics.
explanation.walkthrough: A vulgar fraction is an ordinary fraction like three-quarters; the joke is that anything vulgar is unwelcome where everything is pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical mathematics studied for its own sake, without practical application, is the abstract science named.

clue.text: Struggle in which the Services prove decisive

definitions.text: Struggle in which the Services prove decisive

parts.words: Struggle in which the Services prove decisive
parts.note: reads like a war won by the armed forces, but the services are serves in a tennis contest

explanation.surface: A conflict in which the Army, Navy and Air Force win the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Services' look like the armed forces; in tennis a server holding serve is decisive in this deciding game.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a deciding game played at six games all is won by the player who wins the points on serve.

clue.text: Dislike having to remove sulphur from silver metal

indicators.note: the chemical symbol for sulphur is taken out of the metal's name

parts.note: sodium is a soft, silvery-white metal
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Someone hates having to clean sulphur tarnish off their silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is not the element Ag here: it describes the silvery colour of SODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is hatred or strong disapproval felt towards someone.

clue.text: The King's mistress is in a state, journalist is in the doghouse!

indicators.note: the mistress sits inside the letters formed by the state and the journalist

parts.note: Ken. is an old abbreviation for Kentucky, a US state
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A royal scandal: the King's lover is in a frenzy and a reporter is in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like 'agitated', but the state is Kentucky; 'is in' signals the container. Doghouse is literal here: where a dog is shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog kennelled is shut up in its kennel, a doghouse.

clue.text: Not a starter in the ocean race

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a racecourse, or a course, is where a race is run

explanation.surface: A yacht that does not start in the transatlantic race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' reads as a competitor at the start, but it is the first dish of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal dish of a meal comes after the opening dish, so it is not the first course.

clue.text: Lincoln has one of these hostelries

definitions.meaning: Lincoln's Inn is one of the four ... of Court, the London legal societies
hostelries are pubs or lodging houses for travellers

explanation.surface: The city of Lincoln boasts a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is not the city or the president but Lincoln's Inn, one of the Inns of Court where English barristers belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln's Inn is one of the legal Inns of Court, and pubs where travellers lodge are also called by this name.

clue.text: The lazy creep is legless!

parts.note: slow can mean idle or sluggish
a worm is a creep, a contemptible person

explanation.surface: An idle sneak is blind drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legless' looks like British slang for very drunk, but this creature literally has no legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The slowworm is a legless lizard that creeps along slowly like a worm.

clue.text: Black sheep's first source of power

indicators.note: the sheep's word goes first, ahead of the word for black

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
jet is a deep glossy black

explanation.surface: The family black sheep is the root of the household's strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black sheep' reads as one phrase, a disgrace to the family; split it into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramjet is a simple jet engine, a means of propulsion for aircraft.

clue.text: Quid, perhaps, for a cormorant

definitions.meaning: a quid is a lump of chewing tobacco; a coarse cut tobacco
a type of cormorant, a seabird

explanation.surface: A pound coin is offered for a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is not the slang for a pound here but a plug of tobacco for chewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse cut tobacco and a crested seabird of the cormorant family share this name.

clue.text: Put down a limit for ordering in colour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for colour

parts.note: a hue is a colour

indicators.note: the letters of a limit are put in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets a ceiling on how much colour may be ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for ordering' gives MILIAT; 'in' signals the container. 'Put down' means belittle, not set down.
explanation.definitionFit: To humiliate someone is to put them down, shaming or belittling them.

clue.text: They confine miscreant finally to the slammer for reform

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word miscreant is taken
reform means the letters of slammer are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A villain is finally sent to prison to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reform' looks like the purpose of prison but rearranges SLAMMER into RAMMELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Trammels are restraints or hindrances, things that hold someone in.

clue.text: A garden in which Ketelbey' wrote

definitions.text: A garden in which Ketelbey' wrote

parts.words: A garden in which Ketelbey' wrote
parts.note: refers to the title of a popular 1915 piece by the composer Albert Ketelbey, about a garden of a religious house

explanation.surface: A composer sat down to work in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Ketèlbey's light orchestral piece is called 'In a Monastery Garden'; the clue supplies all of that title except the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden in the title of the composer's famous piece belonged to a religious community's house where monks live.

clue.text: One missing sliced beans with tea, say

indicators.note: the beans are cut up and their letters reassembled in another order
say means the next word is heard rather than seen, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the drink sounds just like the golf peg

explanation.surface: Someone skipped a meal of cut beans and a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' rearranges BEANS into ABSEN; 'say' turns tea into TEE, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone missing from where they ought to be, such as work or school, is absent.

clue.text: During a stroll, girl is likely to be won over

indicators.note: the girl's name comes during, that is inside, the stroll

parts.note: an amble is a leisurely stroll
Ena is a girl's name, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: On a walk, a young woman is ready to be persuaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is open to persuasion and readily agrees.

clue.text: Having nothing on a dark horse, back the favourite finally

indicators.note: back means the word for the horse is read from right to left

parts.note: a dun is a horse of dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: only the last letter of favourite is taken

explanation.surface: A racegoer bets on an outsider and then backs the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dark horse' means an outsider in racing, but here it is a dun, a dull brown horse, turned around by 'back' to give NUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naked has no clothes on.

clue.text: A Hopi: brave at first perhaps shows fear

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged some other way
only the opening letter of brave is taken

explanation.surface: A Native American warrior seems frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: A Hopi brave is a warrior of the Hopi people; 'perhaps' rearranges A HOPI with B, the first letter of brave.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an irrational, intense dread of something.

clue.text: Suits reported to give satisfaction

indicators.note: reported means the word is spoken out, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: pleas are lawsuits or cases put to a court

explanation.surface: News of a court case is said to have satisfied everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Suits are not clothes but legal actions.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to make them content or happy.

clue.text: Porter right on his toes

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A hotel porter who is quick and attentive.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is the drink, not the doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alert is watchful and ready, as a person on their toes is.

clue.text: Had curious recurrent noise from attachment

indicators.note: curious means the letters of had are set out in an odd order
recurrent means the word noise runs back on itself, read from right to left

explanation.surface: A strange repeating noise comes from a gadget attached to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' rearranges HAD into ADH and 'recurrent' turns NOISE back into ESION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesion is the act of sticking fast, attachment to a surface.

clue.text: Vegetable one put in Stanley's sandwich

indicators.note: the numeral one is put inside the pair of words that frame the name

parts.note: Marmion's dying cry in Scott's poem is 'On, Stanley, on!', so the name is sandwiched between two copies of on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An onion slice goes into the sandwich Stanley is making.
explanation.walkthrough: The sandwich is a quotation: in Walter Scott's poem Marmion the hero dies crying 'Charge, Chester, charge! On, Stanley, on!'
explanation.definitionFit: The bulb is a common pungent vegetable used in cooking.

clue.text: Piece of soap from Dundee?

definitions.meaning: a bar or tablet of soap is called by this name
a Dundee is a rich fruit ... topped with almonds, named after the Scottish city

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bar of soap came from the Scottish city of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a city in Scotland, but the question mark shows it is an example: the Dundee fruit cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A solid block of soap and a Scottish fruit loaf share this name.

clue.text: I'm taken in by clumsy blighter's underhand trick

indicators.note: the letters of I'm are taken into the middle of the rearranged word
clumsy suggests the letters of blighter are put together awkwardly in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
I'm gives its two letters, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone is duped by an awkward scoundrel's sly scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' gives THBLERIG; 'taken in by' signals the container. A thimblerig is the old cups-and-pea swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle in which a pea is hidden under one of three cups is a sleight-of-hand cheat.

clue.text: Order cattle by the head

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle or oxen
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Someone tells the herd to be counted per animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the head' looks like 'per head' but gives the headland NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatness is tidiness, a state of being in good order.

clue.text: Annoy, perhaps finally exasperate, a person of importance.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of annoy might be arranged another way
only the last letter of exasperate is taken

explanation.surface: Irritate, maybe in the end infuriate, a VIP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ANNOY into ANYON.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'everyone who is anyone was there', the word can mean somebody who matters.
